headline: Parks Canada Discovery Pass and Camping Reservations
reservation: While day-use entry typically requires a standard daily fee or a Discovery Pass, camping at Astotin Lake requires a separate advance booking. High demand for summer weekends makes the reservation system a critical bottleneck; check the Parks Canada reservation service for current availability. Vehicle entry is distinct from any specialized interpretive programming bookings.

days.title: Bison and Lakeshore Vistas

stops.name: Yellowhead Highway Bison Loop
stops.detail: Drive the designated loops to spot Plains bison and wood bison in their separate fenced habitats.

stops.name: Astotin Lake
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalks or rent a canoe to explore the islands and observe the diverse waterfowl population.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for the transit from Edmonton and slow interior loops; conditions vary.
days.note: Bison may block roads; remain inside your vehicle and maintain a safe distance at all times.

days.title: Aspen Parkland Trails
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Astotin Lake Recreation Area

stops.name: Moss Lake Trail
stops.detail: Hike through the rolling hills and aspen forest to see the impact of beaver activity on the local hydrology.

stops.name: Shirley Lake Trail
stops.detail: Explore the meadows and wetlands to find elk and moose, which are most active in the early morning or evening.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes between trailheads; conditions vary by trail moisture levels.
days.note: Trails can be muddy after rainfall; allow extra time for the 10km+ loops.

days.title: Dark Sky and Wildlife Viewing

stops.name: Tawayik Lake
stops.detail: Visit this quieter lake area for birdwatching and to see the transition between forest and grassland.

stops.name: Beaver Hills Dark Sky Preserve
stops.detail: Stay late to witness the stars in this internationally recognized preserve, free from urban light pollution.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour total travel; conditions vary by night visibility.
days.note: Evenings require insect protection; the preserve status is best appreciated on cloudless nights.

intel.title: Astotin Lake Hub
intel.text: The largest parking area is at Astotin Lake, which serves as the hub for most activities. Secondary trailheads have much smaller gravel pull-offs that can fill on summer afternoons.

intel.title: Moderate Coverage
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally stable along the Yellowhead Highway but can become spotty in the southern trail sections. Emergency phones are located at major facility clusters.

intel.title: Gateway Gas
intel.text: There are no fueling stations within the park boundaries. Fill your tank in Sherwood Park or Fort Saskatchewan before entering the park gates.

intel.title: Dawn and Dusk Wildlife
intel.text: Bison and elk are most active during the cooler hours of early morning and late evening. Afternoon heat often drives wildlife into the deeper forest shade.

intel.title: Fenced Boundaries
intel.text: The entire park is fenced to manage the bison herds; ensure all gates are properly closed if using backcountry access points. Some trails may close seasonally for bison handling operations.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Edmonton International Airport (YEG), rent a vehicle, and pick up groceries in Sherwood Park before the short drive east on Highway 16.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are perfect for the paved park roads; RVs are common but should check height clearances at the Astotin Lake campground trees.
plan.goldenHour: Astotin Lake Beach offers a clear westward view for sunsets over the water and islands.
